what: The declarative field manifest both engines compare through. cpu/core/statecompare.ts and gpu/core/statecompare.py each implement an extractor per (group, field) NAME; a name in this file with no extractor, or an extractor with no name here, is a hard error rather than a silently missing column.

compare.exact: an integer-valued fact. The two engines must produce the same integer. Folded into the group's `exact` digest.
compare.milli: a float accumulator. Quantised to milli-units (JS Math.round of value*1000) and folded into the group's separate `milli` digest, so a float disagreement is reported apart from an integer one. A hash cannot carry a tolerance, which is why the two are separate digests rather than one.

gap: A field carrying `gap` is a KNOWN cross-engine storage asymmetry: both extractors exist and the census counts the field as covered, but the default digest skips it because it is guaranteed to disagree until the gap closes. Turning them on is a per-field decision, not a policy.

keys.per-seat: one row per CIV seat; key = the absolute seat id (cpu/core/seats.ts)
keys.per-city-state: one row per living city-state; key = its id
keys.per-city: one row per living city of any civ seat; key = the city's CENTER TILE index — globally unique, stable across capture, and stored by both engines. Slot index, founding order and array position are all engine-local and none of them is a valid join.
keys.per-unit: one row per living unit; key = tileIndex * 2 + (civilian ? 1 : 0). Both engines allow at most one military and one civilian unit per tile (the GPU's military_at/civilian_at pair), so the pair is unique. `game.unitCount` guards the assumption: two units colliding on one key would merge silently in the digest but change the count.
keys.per-tile: one row per map tile; key = the tile index

fields.name: emergencyTable
fields.note: sorted by (kind, target, city) and padded to EMERGENCY_SLOTS: the TS list is an array in trigger order, the GPU a fixed slot table, so slot POSITION is not a shared fact. Members and affected seats ride as bitmasks.

fields.name: pantheonsClaimed
fields.note: the global COUNT; which pantheon each seat took is the per-seat `beliefPantheon` field, and the claim mask is that set

fields.name: beliefsClaimed
fields.note: TS keeps ONE claimedBeliefs list mixing follower and founder ids; the GPU counts the two pools separately. The comparison is over the total, because splitting the TS list needs the belief catalogs and the total is the fact both engines actually agree on.

fields.name: enhancerBeliefsClaimed
fields.note: the global COUNT; which enhancer each seat took is the per-seat `beliefEnhancer` field, and the claim mask is that set

fields.name: greatPeopleByClass
fields.note: great people are drawn from ONE global pool on both engines, so the per-class QUEUE POSITION is a game-level fact, not a per-seat one. It is the position and not the count because the queue steps past anyone the world era has left behind; `claimedGreatPeople` is the id list that position walks.

fields.name: barbCamps
fields.note: camp TILES, sorted. Only the barbarian seat holds camps; every other seat's list is empty by rule, which is why this is one game-level field instead of a per-seat one.

fields.name: cityCount
fields.note: guards the per-city key: two cities colliding on one center tile would merge in the city digest and change nothing else.

fields.name: explored
fields.note: per-seat fog, dense 0/1 over tiles. TS's empty array (nothing revealed yet) renders dense-zero; every seat reveals at its t0 spawn, so the empty state never reaches a digest.

fields.name: emergencyRewards
fields.note: what a resolved emergency leaves standing, forever. Counters rather than a list of past emergencies: winning the same kind twice pays twice.

fields.name: techs
fields.note: the SET of researched tech indices, not the count — a count cannot tell two different trees of the same size apart.

fields.name: boosted
fields.note: both boost masks, tech then civic, in one vector

fields.name: wars
fields.note: the set of ABSOLUTE opponent seat ids, so a civ/civ war, a civ/city-state war and a civ/barbarian war are the same fact in the same field.

fields.name: warWeariness
fields.note: per-opponent, as (opponent seat, points) pairs sorted by opponent — the sum and the max both cancel a pair of opposite errors.

fields.name: capitalTile
fields.note: one seat-indexed plane; row 0 starts -1 (no capital yet) while civ rows are zero-initialised, so an unfounded civ seat reads tile 0 rather than 'none'.

fields.name: religionFounded
fields.note: read off holy_tile >= 0 on the GPU: the holy tile is written exactly when a religion is founded, and it is the only founding record seat 0 has.

fields.name: pantheonDone
fields.note: the GPU keeps a DONE bit beside the chosen id; this side has only the id, so the comparison is `pantheon !== null` vs `civ_pantheon_done`

fields.name: enhancerDone
fields.note: the GPU keeps a DONE bit beside the chosen id; this side has only the id, so the comparison is `enhancer != null` vs `civ_enhancer_done`

fields.name: routeCount
fields.note: count only — route IDENTITY is the `routes` field beside it

fields.name: routes
fields.note: per-route [fromTile, destTile, kind, expiresTurn, createdTurn, walkTile, walkLeg], sorted; destinations in CENTRE-TILE space because city ids are not compared. The walk triple IS the Trader while it services the route.

fields.name: tilesPurchased
fields.gap: seat 0's row of `civ_tiles_purchased` exists but nothing writes it until the seat-0 purchase wire; comparison opens with it.

fields.name: envoys
fields.note: a vector over civ seats in seat order — one store for every seat, which is what makes the suzerain contest one comparison.

fields.name: questDistrict
fields.gap: Both engines DERIVE the asked district (a kind-3 quest always asks the CS type's own): TS digests PLACEABLE_DISTRICTS.indexOf(quest.district), the GPU digests _citystate_didx (a districts_cat index). Different lists — the numbers only agree where the orders coincide.

fields.name: buildings
fields.note: the SET of building indices in cpu/core/prodLayout.ts order — the order rules.json ships and the GPU's city_bldg column order.

fields.name: specialists
fields.note: effectiveSpecialists per PLACEABLE district: the pinned citizens plus the automatic overflow, derived live on both engines.

fields.name: specialistPref
fields.note: how many citizens the player PINNED into each district's slots, by PLACEABLE district index; -1 = the automatic rule decides.

fields.name: queueFront
fields.note: the front item as a production-layout column plus its target tile. The GPU queue is depth ONE — city_current holds a single item — so anything TS has queued behind the front has no twin to compare.

fields.name: artifactProv
fields.note: era and civilization per artifact SLOT — the theming rule's inputs

fields.name: gwArtProv
fields.note: art TYPE and the ARTIST who made it, per ART MUSEUM slot — the other theming rule's inputs

fields.name: seat
fields.note: `unit_alive` is the row filter for the whole unit group (group_rows), not a column of this field

fields.name: type
fields.note: the roster index — cpu/core/prodLayout.ts rosterUnitIds() order, which IS rules.json's units order and the GPU's unit_type space.

fields.name: charges
fields.note: TS spells 'not a builder' as null and the GPU as 0; both are read as 0 here, so the field compares charge COUNT, never the builder/non-builder distinction (which `type` already carries).

fields.name: movesLeft
fields.gap: the GPU's unit_mp/unit_mp_full pair is maintained but is not yet the movement source of truth — the walkers still carry the remainder in locals — so between phases the two engines answer 'how much movement is left' from different places.

fields.name: ownerCity
fields.note: ONE ownerCity beside ownerSeat on both engines: `tile_city` carries the owning city's id for every seat, in that seat's own city-id space; `tile_seat` says whose.

fields.name: improvement
fields.note: index into rules.improvements.ids (cpu/core/unitActions.ts IMPROVEMENT_IDS), -1 = none.

fields.name: district
fields.note: index into PLACEABLE_DISTRICTS, -1 = none.

fields.name: builtWonder
fields.note: index into cpu/core/prodLayout.ts wonderIds(), -1 = none.

fields.name: antiquityProv
fields.note: a dig remembers its era and its civilization; cleared with the site

fields.name: shipwreckProv
fields.note: the wreck's provenance, same shape as the land dig's

fields.name: locked
fields.note: the citizen PINNED to this plot — the work ranking takes every locked plot before it ranks anything by score

fields.name: hasFeature
fields.note: PRESENCE only. The GPU keeps the feature id in a static plane (feat_id) and records removal with feat_stripped, so 'which feature' would need the fixture's t0 ids on the TS side; 'is there one' is fully determined by live state on both engines and is what a chop changes.

fields.name: hasResource
fields.note: PRESENCE only, for the same reason as hasFeature: a district pave strips a BONUS resource and res_stripped is how the GPU records it.

gpu.why: THIS TURN's World Congress ballot. Written inside seatPhase and cleared by worldCongress at the turn tail whether a session fires or not, so it is never live at a turn boundary and there is no TS field to compare it against.

the winner is DERIVED, not stored, on the TS side — domination first, else the score leader once the game is over, recomputed per read. Comparing the GPU's cache means recomputing that derivation in the adapter, which is exactly what gpu-trace.ts's `winner` column already does. The manifest describes STATE; derived quantities are compared by the observation and by the trace.
